findings.classification: Strongly supported by source state transition; not reproduced on Windows
findings.evidence: The End handler sets script:StopRequested=true. On Stop-Service timeout/error it displays Needs attention but never clears that flag. The next 2-second timer tick sees a still-running service, passes StopRequested=true to Get-TrayState, which unconditionally returns Stopping; Set-TrayState disables the End action in that state.
findings.impact: After a failed shutdown, the tray returns to Stopping and disables retrying End although no shutdown is in progress; user must use another control/restart the monitor to retry.
findings.recommendation: Clear StopRequested on failed shutdown or derive Stopping from ShutdownInProgress, preserving an enabled retry action when an error leaves the service running.
findings.validation: Static trace of End catch -> timer tick -> Get-TrayState -> Set-TrayState; Windows PowerShell/WinForms and WSL were unavailable, so no live reproduction or built-in -SelfCheck executed.

findings.title: Failed shutdown leaves the tray in a persistent Stopping state with End disabled
findings.classification: Strongly supported by source state transition; no live Windows reproduction
findings.trigger: End is clicked, Stop-Service throws or reaches its failure deadline, and the GUI/backend remains observable as running on the next timer tick.
findings.evidence: End sets script:StopRequested=true. The catch sets Needs attention without resetting the flag. Timer passes StopRequested to Get-TrayState; true immediately returns Stopping. Set-TrayState disables End for Stopping.

source_derived_transition.step: Next timer tick sees running service

findings.impact: The normal retry control is disabled after a failure although no shutdown call remains active. The error balloon and brief Needs attention state are overwritten by the monitor.
change_surface: Voice Tray.ps1: End click handler, persistent error/intent state, timer Get-TrayState input and Set-TrayState action policy
Voice Tray.ps1 -SelfCheck or a separate Windows test harness for failure->tick->retry; keep tests local and mocked
repair_steps: Define separate meanings for requested stop, active shutdown, and failed shutdown. Avoid using a permanently latched intent as the active-operation indicator.
On failed Stop-Service, reset the active/requested state as needed for retry and retain an error/Needs attention condition until acknowledged/retried or resolved.
Make the next timer tick preserve an actionable failure state while the runtime still runs; allow another End action once ShutdownInProgress is false.
Keep the existing ShutdownInProgress guard to prevent overlapping shutdown calls and preserve the monitor's successful-stop exit policy.
Extend state tests to invoke a fake failing shutdown and then the same timer decision path; test a second successful attempt.
Validate the narrow change on Windows PowerShell/WinForms, then on an isolated verified owned WSL deployment.
invariants: End is disabled only while an actual shutdown is in progress, not indefinitely after an error.
A failed stop remains visible/actionable through subsequent timer ticks.
Two concurrent stop operations are not started.
A successful shutdown still verifies process, health/readiness, ports and ownership lease removal before reporting completion.
Tray controls stop only the managed GUI/application path; do not introduce broad process termination or named-container stops.
Closing/reopening the dedicated Edge app does not target unrelated browser profiles.
acceptance: Mock Stop-Service failure with health/background still running: immediately after catch and after at least two timer ticks, state is Needs attention and End remains enabled.
A second End click actually invokes Stop-Service again; on success monitor exits normally.
While fake Stop-Service is in progress, End remains disabled and duplicate invocation is rejected.
Original startup timeout, never-started monitor, health-but-unready state and successful-stop exit behavior still pass.
An error balloon/message explains the failure without being contradicted by a permanently spinning Stopping label.
regression_scenarios: Shutdown timeout while GUI health stays 200
Native WSL command failure before interrupt is delivered
GUI process gone but backend/port/ownership checks still prevent completed shutdown
Failure followed by a successful retry
Failure followed by spontaneous runtime exit
User double-clicks End / overlapping UI events
Existing startup, ready/unready and monitor exit cases in -SelfCheck
risks: StopRequested also participates in Should-ExitMonitor, so changing its lifecycle can affect monitor exit timing; inspect both uses.
A simplistic state reset can replace Needs attention with Running on the next poll despite unresolved shutdown verification; preserve error visibility intentionally.
Live stop/retry tests act on a real runtime; use a verified disposable owned instance and avoid unrelated containers or user data.
findings.rollback: Revert only the tray state correction if native lifecycle behavior regresses. Retain normal -StopOnly as the documented managed control where ownership is verified; preserve all user/deployment data.
